description: How every plane reads the address a frame reaches its self-hosted backend on. The stored form is three fields — server_host (a bare host, no scheme, port or path), server_port and server_scheme (frame.json serverHost / serverPort / serverScheme) — and the scheme is never guessed from the port once stated. `schemeFromPort` is the ONE seed rule for a row or frame.json written before server_scheme existed (2026.9.13): https when the port ends in 443 (443, 8443, 1443), http otherwise. `normalizeScheme` is what a stored value becomes (trailing `://` tolerated, junk falls back to the seed). `splitAddress` is what a typed address becomes wherever one is accepted (the add-frame and adopt forms, the frame settings' host field, the Wi-Fi portal, the device's own frame API, frame.json on load): scheme '' and port null mean 'not said' and the consumer fills them. A port that is not a number (`user:pw@host`) and a scheme other than http or https stay in the host so the host check refuses the whole thing. Replayed by backend/app/utils/tests/test_server_address.py, frameos/src/frameos/tests/test_server_address.nim, cloud/apps/auth-web/src/test/shared-spa/backend-address.test.ts and ios/FrameOSKit/Tests/FrameOSKitTests/ServerAddressTests.swift (the iOS app's self-hosted sign-in reads the typed backend address with it).
